subject: Dedicated pool sizing for long-window model — context packing & precision tradeoffs
messages:
From: Nick Porter <nick.porter@synthera.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity for 64k context genomics pipeline

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Synthera is sizing a private deployment to run our annotation pipeline and a few research assistants that use very long documents (up to 64k tokens). We have two model candidates: an open 70B variant and a 13B custom fine-tune. Key asks:

- Rough reserved GPU capacity needed (pods / GPUs) for the production traffic profile below.
- How much memory is consumed by the KV cache for the long-window sessions and how that changes with 8-bit or 4-bit quantization.
- Any guidance on quality tradeoffs if we push to 4-bit for the 70B model.

Traffic profile (initial): 20 concurrent endpoints (steady), 200 requests/minute peak, average generation length 800 tokens, peak context load occasional bumps to 64k when researchers use long-session recall.

We can share example prompts. Would prefer a short written sizing before we lock in a Dedicated contract.

Best,
Nick Porter
CTO, Synthera Labs

Hi Nick — thanks, this is great context.

Quick response with recommended next steps and a preliminary sizing attached (synthera_kv_memory_modeling.xlsx):

1) We did a first-pass model-by-model memory and pod-count estimate using your profile and conservative headroom (30%). Attachment includes the per-request memory envelope and a per-pod concurrency assumption.

2) Short answers now:
- KV cache: scales roughly linearly with context length; for your 70B-class model we estimate ~0.9–1.1 GB per 1k tokens in baseline FP16 execution (model + KV on-GPU).
- Quantization: moving to 8-bit execution typically reduces model weights footprint and KV store by ~45–55% (so ~0.45–0.6 GB per 1k). 4-bit can often get you an additional ~30–40% reduction versus 8-bit but requires validated kernels and can affect generation quality for the 70B variant.

3) We’re looping in Rishi (infrastructure) and Monica (customer success) to validate the pod-level assumptions and propose a Dedicated pool config (GPU type, pod memory, and autoscaling knobs).

I attached the spreadsheet with the conservative scenario and an optimistic quantized-run scenario. If you’re available later today we can jump on a short call to walk the numbers.

Cheers,

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Nick Porter <nick.porter@synthera.com>

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 9:04 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Nick — thanks, this is great context.
> 
> Quick response with recommended next steps and a preliminary sizing attached (synthera_kv_memory_modeling.xlsx):

Nick / Stephanie — I validated the spreadsheet and added a technical appendix (short notes below) with conservative per-GPU numbers. High-level takeaways first, then the numbers:

High-level:
- For the 70B-class model (baseline FP16), expect a single GPU to host the model weights + execution state if you choose an A100-80GB or equivalent; however, once you add a 64k KV cache per concurrent session the effective memory pressure grows and you'll need to partition sessions across GPUs (or use KV offload strategies).
- With 8-bit quantization (we tested per-channel INT8-like flows and 8-bit GEMM kernels), model weights + KV memory demand typically drops ~50%. This often enables the 70B variant to fit comfortably on an 80GB GPU with multiple concurrent shorter sessions, but not many simultaneous 64k sessions.
- 4-bit (QLoRA-style 4-bit weights + 4-bit KV packing) reduces memory further and can allow a 70B-like execution on a 48GB-class card for single-user long sessions, but quality must be validated for your biology prompts — we recommend blind A/B evals before committing.

Numbers / assumptions used (conservative):
- Model param footprint (FP16, 70B): ~140 GB raw -> sharded/paged to GPU results in ~70–80 GB resident depending on kernel memory reuse.
- Model param footprint (8-bit): effective resident ~36–42 GB. (assumes activation recompute remains FP16 where applicable)
- KV cache growth: FP16 KV ~= 1.0 GB per 1k tokens for this architecture. 8-bit KV ~= 0.5–0.55 GB per 1k. 4-bit KV ~= 0.32–0.38 GB per 1k.
- Example: 64k context KV on GPU -> FP16: ~64 * 1.0 = ~64 GB; 8-bit: ~32–35 GB; 4-bit: ~20–24 GB.

Pod sizing examples (conservative, includes OS + runtime overhead ~6–8 GB):
- Option A (FP16, 70B): 1x A100-80GB per replica; supports 1–2 short concurrent sessions (<=8k) but cannot hold multiple 64k users concurrently. For your steady 20 concurrent endpoints with frequent long-session spikes we project needing ~18–24 GPUs to keep headroom and concurrency SLAs.
- Option B (INT8/8-bit, 70B variant): 1x A100-80GB or 2x 48GB cards with NVLink for shard-friendly configs; supports up to 6–8 concurrent short sessions and 2–3 concurrent 64k sessions depending on traffic shaping; projected pool size ~8–12 GPUs for your traffic profile (with 30% headroom).
- Option C (4-bit + KV packing, 70B): feasible on 48GB-class GPUs for single long sessions; for your production concurrency expect ~10–14 48GB GPUs with strict routing rules (long sessions pinned to dedicated subset).

13B variant (baseline FP16): model resident ~10–12 GB; KV scales same way but absolute numbers much smaller — 64k FP16 KV ~64 GB still dominates if you keep KV on GPU. For 13B we recommend using quantized 8-bit which will let you run many more concurrent 64k sessions per GPU. Example: 13B + 8-bit KV -> per 64k session KV ~32–35 GB + model ~6GB -> fit 1–2 sessions per 48GB GPU depending on offload.

Operational recommendations:
- For predictable SLAs, carve a dedicated "long-window" pool in Dedicated (subset of GPU pool) pinned to quantized runtime (8-bit); route known research workloads there and reserve headroom for spikes.
- Use KV offload to host rarely-accessed prefixes on host memory/SSD for extremely long history workflows; this reduces GPU count at the expense of tail latency.
- Canary quality test of 4-bit on a representative prompt set (we can help set up A/B harness) before you commit to 4-bit in production for 70B.

I'll add the per-GPU math into the Drive spreadsheet and flag the cells that change under different quant settings.

—Rishi

Nick — quick summary and next steps (per Rishi’s notes):

Summary:
- Baseline FP16 70B is very memory hungry for 64k sessions; naive pool would be large (18–24 GPUs).
- 8-bit execution is the sweet spot operationally: halves memory and reduces Dedicated GPU footprint to roughly one third of FP16 scenario for your profile (~8–12 GPUs projected).
- 4-bit gives bigger wins but needs validation on biology prompts. We recommend a phased approach: start Dedicated with an 8-bit long-window pool and run a controlled 4-bit canary (we’ll help).

Action items:
- Stephanie: schedule 45m sizing call and walk through the attached spreadsheet (I’ll send a calendar invite).
- Rishi: finalize the per-GPU math in the Drive file and add an example autoscaler policy for long-window pool.
- Monica: prepare a Dedicated proposal (term, pricing tiers, SLAs) using deal id DEAL-2027-SYN-47 and include optional add-on for extended KV offload retention.
- Nick: please share a small set of representative prompts (5–10) so we can run 8-bit vs 4-bit quality checks during the canary.

Proposed times: Fri 16:30–17:15 PT or Mon 10:00–10:45 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.
